zh.caseTitle: 案件：一份「咖啡延寿」的报道
zh.testimony: 各大媒体争相报道：一项针对科技公司年轻员工的研究发现，每天喝三杯以上咖啡的人，体检指标明显更健康。研究团队表示，咖啡中的抗氧化物能延缓衰老，所以多喝咖啡可以延年益寿。至于不喝咖啡的对照组，样本太少，被排除在分析之外。

textRefs.spot_samplebias: 一项针对科技公司年轻员工的研究
textRefs.spot_corr: 咖啡中的抗氧化物能延缓衰老，所以多喝咖啡可以延年益寿
textRefs.spot_control: 不喝咖啡的对照组，样本太少，被排除在分析之外
textRefs.debunk_samplebias: 样本偏差：只调查年轻健康的科技公司员工，结论却推广到全体人群——样本无法代表你要下的结论。
textRefs.debunk_corr: 相关≠因果：喝咖啡的人更健康，可能是他们本来生活习惯就更好，也可能方向反了——「体检更好」与「喝咖啡」的关系需要实验验证。
textRefs.debunk_control: 缺乏对照：把唯一的对照组排除掉，等于自己取消了「比较」——没有对照就没有因果判断。
textRefs.q_samplebias: 只研究年轻白领，结论能代表老人、病人或体力劳动者吗？
textRefs.q_corr: 喝咖啡和体检更健康，谁是因谁是果？有没有第三因素？
textRefs.q_control: 为什么把对照组排除？不喝咖啡的人数据如何？

hints: 样本是谁？能代表结论覆盖的全体吗？
没有对照组的比较，等于没有比较
zh.explanation: 这篇「咖啡延寿」报道有三处硬伤：①样本只来自年轻健康的科技公司员工，却推广到所有人；②相关关系被说成因果关系；③把对照组排除在分析外。看研究结论记住三问：样本代表谁？相关还是因果？对照组在哪？

en.caseTitle: Case: A Report Claiming "Coffee Extends Life"
en.testimony: Major media are reporting: a study of young employees at tech companies found that people who drink more than three cups of coffee a day have noticeably healthier checkup results. The research team says the antioxidants in coffee slow aging, so drinking more coffee extends life. As for the non-coffee-drinking control group, the sample was too small and was excluded from the analysis.

textRefs.spot_samplebias: a study of young employees at tech companies
textRefs.spot_corr: the antioxidants in coffee slow aging, so drinking more coffee extends life
textRefs.debunk_samplebias: Sample bias: only young, healthy tech employees were studied, yet the conclusion is generalized to everyone — the sample cannot represent the claim's population.
textRefs.debunk_corr: Correlation is not causation: coffee drinkers being healthier may mean they already had better habits, or the direction could be reversed — "healthier checkups" and "coffee" need an experiment to untangle.
textRefs.debunk_control: No control: excluding the only control group cancels the comparison itself — without a control there is no causal judgment.
textRefs.q_samplebias: Studying only young white-collar workers — can the conclusion represent the elderly, the sick, or manual laborers?
textRefs.q_corr: Between coffee and better checkups, which is the cause? Could a third factor drive both?
textRefs.q_control: Why was the control group excluded? What do the non-drinkers' numbers show?
textRefs.q_d1: How many years did this study run?
textRefs.q_d2: What brand of coffee was used?

hints: Who is in the sample? Can it represent the population of the conclusion?
A comparison without a control group is no comparison at all
en.explanation: This "coffee extends life" report has three hard flaws: ① the sample only covers young, healthy tech employees yet is generalized to everyone; ② correlation is dressed up as causation; ③ the control group was excluded from the analysis. When reading any study, remember three questions: who does the sample represent? correlation or causation? where is the control group?
